requirements.summary: nfs-kernel-server installed and active on node1; /etc/exports configured for /srv/nfs/shared restricted to node2's IP with rw,sync,no_subtree_check,root_squash; exportfs -v confirms the export is live, and showmount -e from node2 confirms visibility. Export and service remained active after a full node1 restart.

requirements.requirement: Mount the export at /mnt/shared on node2
requirements.summary: fstab entry added on node2 for the NFS export at /mnt/shared; mount -a succeeded and mount output confirms an active nfs4 mount. Mount persisted correctly (via fstab auto-mount) and remained functional after a full node2 restart, with correct ownership/mode.

requirements.requirement: Shared identity dataops with UID/GID 4500 created on both node1 and node2
requirements.summary: groupadd/useradd created dataops with uid=4500 gid=4500 on both node1 and node2, confirmed via id command output on each node.

requirements.requirement: Shared directory set to dataops:dataops with mode 2770
requirements.summary: chown/chmod applied on node1's /srv/nfs/shared; ls -la and stat show drwxrws--- dataops dataops (mode 2770) both on the server side and as seen through the mount on node2, including after node2's restart.

requirements.requirement: Files created on either system keep consistent ownership/permissions on the other
requirements.summary: A file created as dataops on node2 (from_node2.txt) appeared with dataops:dataops ownership on node1, and a file created on node1 (from_node1.txt) appeared with dataops:dataops ownership on node2's mount; directory mode 2770 preserved on both sides.

overall_summary: All material outcomes of the task contract were directly and coherently demonstrated: NFS export of /srv/nfs/shared on node1, persistent mount at /mnt/shared on node2, matching dataops (UID/GID 4500) identities on both nodes, dataops:dataops ownership with mode 2770 on the shared directory, and consistent cross-node file ownership/permissions verified in both directions. The executor additionally ran the provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol on both nodes, capturing healthy baselines, restart acknowledgements, changed boot identities (cross-checked against the fixed lifecycle snapshots, which match exactly), and full recovery of services, mount, and data with correct ownership — directly demonstrating the health-through-disruption-to-recovery transition rather than relying on configuration alone. Temporary test artifacts were cleaned up, leaving the share empty as expected. No unnecessary or unreverted mutations were found.
limitations: Task-level restart/persistence was not explicitly required by the contract, but the executor's restart evidence happens to also validate export/mount persistence across a reboot, strengthening confidence in requirement satisfaction beyond what the base task demanded.

Evidence for NFS protocol version in use (mount shows nfs4) was not cross-checked against the export's supported versions in the exports file, though this is a minor implementation detail not specified by the task.

operational_hygiene.summary: Reviewed the full executor command timeline chronologically. All state-changing commands map clearly to task prerequisites (user/group creation, package install, directory setup, export/mount configuration) or to bounded, fully-reverted verification steps. Test files created for cross-node ownership checks (from_node2.txt, from_node1.txt) were removed at cmd-393f53852cdd4072. Restart-protocol test files (baseline_node1.txt, post_node1_restart.txt, post_node2_restart.txt) were removed at cmd-02b2fd0608c2434c, leaving the share directory empty as intended. The stale dpkg lock on node1 was investigated read-only (fuser/lsof) then resolved with dpkg --configure -a, a corrective action with no lasting side effect beyond completing pending package configuration. The two shutdown -r now restarts are bounded, task-adjacent (part of the mandated node-restart evidence protocol) and both nodes returned to full working order afterward.
